A little note from present-day me

Little designer me, taking on big designs for the first time. Would I approach some things differently today? Absolutely. But I’m proud of her ambition—and the work she put into figuring it out. That’s why this project has a place here.

01 / The challenge

Convey. Turn. Direct.

Parcel handling needs a way to keep items moving while directing them to different destinations. My thesis explored a swing-wheel sorting module that combines a driven wheel surface with a mechanism for changing wheel direction.

I developed SolidWorks assembly and component drawings, documented power-transmission calculations, and proposed a sensor-based PLC control architecture. The modular concept allows the sorting surface to be adapted in length and width.

Scope of the work
This case study presents the engineering design and its documentation. The control architecture is proposed; physical commissioning, throughput, and sorting accuracy are not established by the supplied project records.
01 / TRANSPORT

Drive the wheel surface

A motor-driven transmission and polyurethane belts deliver rotation to the conveying wheels.

02 / ORIENT

Change the wheel direction

The swing mechanism adjusts wheel orientation to change the parcel’s travel direction.

03 / COORDINATE

Connect sensing and motion

The proposed controls coordinate parcel detection, conveyor motion, and the sorting operation.

02 / Mechanical evidence

From assembly to individual parts.

The drawing package includes two assembly sheets and eleven component or subassembly sheets. Section views expose the drive arrangement; detail drawings document dimensions, fits, and surface-finish requirements.

03 / Power transmission

Connect motion requirements to a drive.

The thesis develops working-speed, transmission-ratio, belt-drive, motor, and bearing calculations. One example is the relationship between the selected motor speed and the calculated working speed.

Design calculation / Speed reduction
960 / 76.39 ≈ 12.57
Input speed / working speed = total transmission ratio

Distributing the reduction

The study allocates a belt-drive ratio of 3 and a remaining reduction of approximately 4.19. These are documented design values, rather than measured operating results.

Source: thesis, Chapter IV, transmission-ratio calculations.
04 / Automation concept

A mechanical module within a control system.

The thesis proposes a Siemens S7-200-based system integrating sensing, conveyor drives, and operator interaction. These elements describe the intended architecture rather than a commissioned PLC installation.

Detection

Sensors provide parcel presence and position information for the control sequence.

Control & drives

PLC coordination and frequency-converter control connect the handling stations and conveyor motion.

Operator interface

A proposed touchscreen interface supports system monitoring and interaction.

05 / Reflection

What this project brought together.

The study connected machine design, CAD documentation, power transmission, and automation within one material-handling problem. Its strongest portfolio evidence is the assembly-to-component drawing package.

Engineering skills demonstrated

SolidWorks assembly documentation; orthographic and sectional views; component dimensioning; transmission-ratio calculations; belt and bearing selection studies; and a proposed PLC/sensor architecture.

How I would develop the design further

Recheck component sizing and assumptions, verify interfaces and clearances, build a control sequence with defined fault handling, and validate the design through prototyping and measured tests.
